source_review.notes: Reviewed current official Boost Graph concepts/storage/adjacency/edge-list contracts, current NetworkX simple/multigraph documentation, GraphBLAS C 2.1.0, current Redis source as a synchronized-index example, and primary GAP/GBBS benchmark papers. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200. A stale Boost documentation root returning 404 was replaced with the current official graph-concepts page before review.

evidence: Checked G=(V,E), n/m, ordered versus unordered endpoints, edge identity, incidences, in/out degree, matrix cell semantics, density, and canonical membership.
Checked logical edges, adjacency incidences, physical records, tombstones, descriptors, and derived indices remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Loop and degree conventions are explicitly attached to directed/undirected models rather than assumed universal.

evidence: Recomputed five vertices, seven live directed edges, six nonzero matrix cells, 25 matrix slots, multiplicity two at 0->1, and one at loop 1->1.
Recomputed outgoing degrees 2,2,2,1,0 and incoming degrees 1,3,1,1,1; both sums equal seven.
Recomputed weight-at-most-three IDs e2,e3,e5 and exact deletion of parallel e1 leaving multiplicity one and six live edges.
Checked bit/value matrix byte examples and directed out+in/undirected incidence multiplication formulas.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Python exact integers avoid fixed-width overflow; matrix/offset/capacity/byte overflow is reviewed but not executed.

evidence: Verified matrix O(n^2) storage and row traversal, adjacency degree-sized traversal plus subcontainer-specific membership, and edge-array O(m) scan boundaries.
Verified directed and undirected logical-edge/incidence accounting, loop contributions, and the need for edge IDs under parallelism.
Verified conversions can preserve only semantics encoded by the target, and capability interfaces determine algorithm applicability.
Verified combined representations require canonical-to-derived equality and atomic/versioned publication.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Compressed sparse representations and their offset/sortedness proofs are reserved for DSE-042.

evidence: Reviewed zero/isolated vertices, empty graphs, loops, parallel/opposite edges, simple-graph duplicate policies, one/all parallel deletion, and vertex renumbering.
Reviewed zero/negative/NaN/extreme weights, absence ambiguity, matrix/cell/count/2m/byte overflow, hub skew, capacity slack, tombstone growth, and descriptor invalidation.

Reviewed malformed endpoints/IDs/counts/symmetry/properties/offsets, hash flooding, range amplification, partial out/in publication, snapshot drift, reclamation, crash/recovery, and schema/comparator changes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Logical counts, physical counts, incidences, nonzero cells, allocated capacity, and output volume are independently bounded.

evidence: The executable derives the live edge-ID set from canonical records and checks its cardinality against live_edges.
Every out and in incidence is checked for live membership and matching source/target; both seen sets must equal the canonical live set.
A fresh multiplicity matrix is rebuilt from outgoing incidences and compared exactly after deleting one parallel edge.
invariant_checking.notes: The trace covers one directed multigraph; undirected, descriptor-generation, property-column, concurrency, and persistence validators are specified but not executed.

evidence: Reviewed graph semantic contract, matrix/list/edge cost derivations, per-vertex container choices, canonical records, identity, and invalidation.
Reviewed direction/transpose, undirected incidence models, combinations/transactions, NetworkX/Boost/GraphBLAS capability boundaries, and actual byte/locality accounting.
Reviewed mutation publication, immutable snapshots, locking/versioning/logical deletion, parallel partitioning/skew, persistence/interchange, input validation, and security.
Reviewed canonical model, exhaustive semantic combinations, loss-aware round trips, fault/concurrency/persistence checks, and representative benchmark methodology.
proof_review.notes: No representation is claimed universally superior from density or asymptotics alone.

evidence: The chapter separates mathematical graph, semantic policy, physical layout, generic capability, lifecycle policy, and measured behavior.
Logical edges, duplicate matrix cells, undirected incidences, edge-array positions, and stable descriptors are never conflated.
Current library/standard behavior is attached to named official references; benchmark papers support methodology rather than universal performance conclusions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The finite synchronized graph is explicitly bounded and not a proof of undirected, concurrent, persistent, compressed, or large-scale behavior.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python trace passed exact sixteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_graph_representation_trace and checks canonical edge records, out/in lists, multiplicity matrix, loop, parallel edges, degrees, scan, and one-edge deletion.
All ten final external destinations and all repository-local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No fixed-width/allocation/failure, undirected, stable-generation, iterator, hash, concurrency, persistence, conversion-memory, cache/TLB/branch, GPU/NUMA, or production graph workload was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed graph semantics first, three base representations, subcontainers, identity, synchronized combinations, direction, conversion, current APIs, GraphBLAS algebra, bytes/locality, concurrency, persistence, security, testing, and selection.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed explicit isolated/loop/parallel/property policy, opaque IDs, per-vertex container and incoming-index needs, tombstone/compaction bounds, descriptor/iterator invalidation, actual and peak bytes, snapshots/versioned publication, bounded parsing, WAL/rebuild, skew/partition telemetry, and tail benchmarks.

pedagogical_review.notes: Begins from graph semantics rather than a memorized sparse/dense slogan, derives representation/access costs and cross-view invariants, includes one reproduced multigraph trace, fifteen misconceptions, ten varied examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Boost, NetworkX, GraphBLAS, Redis, GAP, GBBS, security, performance, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite trace prove neither arbitrary graph/comparator/property semantics, fixed-width/allocation/failure safety, undirected incidence policy, descriptor-generation/iterator stability, compressed-sparse correctness, thread safety/linearizability/snapshot isolation, safe reclamation, durable persistence/crash recovery, lossless arbitrary conversion, production memory/cache/TLB/branch/GPU/NUMA/tail behavior, workload-independent superiority, certification, nor deployment fitness.
